note: Example data: an invented online booking software company with invented accounts, not a real business. Every number in expected_output.json follows from this input. Large tables are stored as one comma-separated line per row, in the order of 'columns'.
request: Hey Claude, I just added the "seo-audit" skill. Audit example.com and tell me the five fixes that matter most.
business: Example Booking Software, an online booking and scheduling app for small service businesses (invented example)
pages_that_matter: not given, so the About page and the 7 pages with the most impressions were used
data_pulled: crawler: robots-txt-checker, ssl-certificate-checker, security-headers-checker, status-code-checker (30 URLs: 4 host variants, 16 GA4 landing pages (the top 15 by sessions plus ties; the home page is also a host variant), the top 10 Search Console URLs not in the sitemap and 1 stale redirect error; every audit-set page was already on these lists), meta-tags-checker (gate)

google-search-console: search_analytics by page (158 rows, 154 pages once #fragment rows and trailing-slash twins are merged), check_indexing_issues (top 20), sitemaps_list, batch_url_inspection (30 URLs)
bing-webmaster: get_crawl_stats (data keeps the last 14 days), get_crawl_issues, get_blocked_urls
google-analytics: get_report by landingPage and channel (153 rows)
dataforseo: onpage_instant_pages (9 calls: the audit set and one city page), backlinks_summary (1 call): 10 calls
pagespeed-insights: core-web-vitals on 5 templates, accessibility-seo on the home page, resource-optimizations on the slowest template (/blog/reduce-no-shows/)
sitemap.xml read with a web fetch (177 URLs)
